answer: Clone accounts are filtered by a per-identity bond with slow vesting. Each address must lock stake before bidding on work, and rewards stream out over epochs, so a farm cannot recycle one deposit across many addresses. The bond also anchors a nonce that signs every action, so a cluster of copies leaves one glaring echo in the audit trail. Cloning a hundred bots means posting a hundred real bonds and holding them, so attacker cost climbs linearly while an honest agent's grove of one identity pays a single fee. Slashed bonds drain to a treasury, so the tundra of fakes funds the honest side.
